Beginner Guide: How This Call Trade Works in Plain Dollars

Why this spread works differently from buying shares: BE is in an active Stage 4 correction below its 50D and 200D averages. While buying calls right now at CMP ($187.19) is a trap due to accelerating theta decay on an unconfirmed knife-drop, this defined-risk Bull Call Spread ($185/$270) is structured to be deployed once BE tests its major $161.18 support shelf and stabilizes. Selling the upper $270 call funds your entry, reduces daily theta decay by over 60%, and caps your worst-case loss at $2,286.00.

Exact wallet math (1 contract = 100 shares): You buy the $185 Call for $29.48 and simultaneously sell the $270 Call for $6.62, paying $22.86/sh net ($2,286.00 total for 1 spread(s)). That $2,286.00 is the absolute maximum you can lose.

Breakeven & profit ceiling: At expiry (2027-01-15), you start making money above $207.86 (+11.0% from $187.19). Anywhere at or above $270, your $2,286.00 turns into $8,500.00 (+$6,214.00 net profit).

Speed & time decay in plain English: Today, each $1 move up in BE adds ~$39.20 to your spread (Net Delta), while sitting flat costs ~$7.05/day in time decay (Net Theta) — much lower than an unhedged call because the sold $270 call decays in your favor.
